title: VMF assessment approval
description: ASSESS-PAGE-1: a person's recorded decision that an assessment has been reviewed and a migration may be planned from it. Owner: 'just like azure migrate its a requirement for an assessment (report) prior to any migrate... after the report is reviewed, approved & everything is validated its a run.' Written by Approve-VmfAssessment at approval.json in the assessment; New-VmfPlan refuses an assessment without one. Same shape and the same discipline as wave-approval: the identity comes from the approver's own sign-in and is never typed, and assessmentHash binds the decision to the exact thing that was read.

identity.description: The approver's signed-in Entra identity, captured from their login and never typed. An approval somebody can put a name into is not an approval.

assessmentHash.description: SHA-256 of the assessment document as it was approved. The point is evidence rather than change detection - an assessment cannot be overwritten - so this is what proves WHICH findings a person actually signed off, months later when somebody asks.

note.description: Why, when the approver chose to say. Optional at this gate: approving unlocks planning and changes nothing. The WAVE approval, which authorises a machine being rebuilt, still requires one.

blockedAtApproval.description: How many machines could not migrate when this was approved. Recorded because approving an assessment with blocked machines is a legitimate decision - migrate what can move now - and the record should say that was known rather than leaving it to be inferred.
